title: My Classic Vanilla Cut Out Sugar Cookie recipe, perfect for the holid...
description: My Classic Vanilla Cut Out Sugar Cookie recipe, perfect for the holidays. 🍪🎄 This is what I use for all the sugar cookie art you see here. As a cookie artist, my focus is really on making a cookie that holds its shape, but we can’t abandon flavor and texture either. This is a soft on the inside and slightly crispy on the outside cookie that isn’t too sweet. That’s because it’s made to pair with royal icing. Together, they are perfectly balanced. Enjoy! 1 cup (227 g) or 2 sticks unsalted butter, softened 1 cup (200 g) sugar 1 large egg 2 tsp (10 ml) vanilla extract ¼ tsp baking powder 1 tbsp (8 g) cornstarch  ½ tsp salt 2¾ cups + 1 tbsp (350 g) all-purpose flour *Very abbreviated* instructions: 1. Beat butter and sugar together - just to combine. 2. Add egg and vanilla extract. 3. I like to add my smaller, dry ingredients in before the flour to avoid using another bowl. Add your baking powder, corn starch, and salt. Mix to combine. 4. Add your flour in 3 batches. Mix on low until the dough forms a ball on your paddle. Some dough sticking to the bowl is fine. 5. Chill for at least one hour.  6. Bake at 350F (177F) for 11-12 minutes. #cookiedecorating
transcript: This is the cut out sugar cookie recipe I used for all of my creations and I'm sharing all of my tips so you can make them perfectly. And we're just gonna jump right in, so first things first, do not over mix your butter and sugar. Just mix to combine because if it develops too much air, it's going to cause the cookie to spread. Now when it comes to adding the flour, you do want to mix it for a little bit longer after the ingredients have fully combined because developing a little bit more gluten is going to help the cookie keep its shape. So all in all, don't treat this like it's a cake. Tip number three, this has to chill for at least one hour. Preferably overnight, preferably two nights. Now I don't know the science behind this, but I found the longer you let the dough chill, the better it holds its shape. So take that as you will. Tip number four, flour the heck out of your dough and your rolling pin. This will help prevent bubbles. After I've rolled out my dough, I like to use as much space as possible to cut out my shapes. And then I put them in the freezer for at least 10 minutes. It makes them easier to handle and then I can spread out my cookies once it's ready to bake. These bake for about 11 minutes, but I always check them at the seven minute mark and this is when you want to rotate your sheets, switch racks or even do a little bit of jizzing. And I know this seems very technical, but technically this is a technical cookie. It needs to hold its shape while still being soft on the inside, just crispy on the outside and delicious.
